pages.title: 1. Introduction
pages.markdown:
Welcome to the tutorial of Oncogenomics. Oncogenomics is a web-based portal for displaying cancer analysis results such as variant calls, copy number analysis, gene fusion and RNAseq expression. Oncogenomics is developed by Dr. Javed Khan's lab at NCI. This portal can visualize results directly from the NGS pipeline: [https://github.com/CCRGeneticsBranch/Oncogenomics_NF_WF](https://github.com/CCRGeneticsBranch/Oncogenomics_NF_WF). 

The mission of the Oncogenomics Section is to harness the power of high throughput genomic and proteomic methods to improve the outcome of children with high-risk metastatic, refractory and recurrent cancers. The research goals are to integrate the data, decipher the biology of these cancers and to identify and validate biomarkers and novel therapeutic targets and to rapidly translate our findings to the clinic. For more information about our research, visit the Oncogenomics Section website.

Oncogenomics has two versions: NIH internal site (available on NIH network): [https://oncogenomics.ccr.cancer.gov/](https://oncogenomics.ccr.cancer.gov) Public site: [https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov)


## Data organization and available features

A **project** groups authorized data. A **patient** can represent a subject or a cell line, and can contain multiple **cases** and assay **samples**. Project-level summaries, case-level details, and sample-level matrices can therefore have different row counts.

The portal also supports a scope-aware chatbot, filtered cohort queries, multi-gene expression and metadata plots, project-level Oncoprint, configured cBioPortal links, ChIP-seq summaries, and selected differential-expression workflows. Features appear only when the deployment and project have the required data and configuration. Start with the [guide index](Home) or [cohort/count definitions](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts).

pages.title: 10. Chatbot and tutorials
pages.markdown:
# Chatbot and tutorial answers

Use the chatbot for questions about authorized cohort data and for help using the portal. Availability depends on the deployment enabling the chatbot.

## Choose the right context

- **Home/global chat:** name the project or cancer type. The assistant resolves it against the cohorts available to your account. If a name has several matches, choose the intended cohort before requesting results.
- **Project Chatbot tab:** the project is fixed by the page. A diagnosis in your question narrows that project rather than silently switching to all projects with that diagnosis.
- **Cancer-type chat:** the diagnosis/cancer type is fixed by the page and results are restricted to authorized data for that cohort.

For general instructions such as "How do I download an expression matrix?", no cohort selection is needed. The assistant searches the tutorial instead of fetching patient records.

## Ask a specific data question

Useful questions state the cohort, assay, gene or fusion pair, filters, and desired output. For example:

- "List RNAseq samples in this project, filtered to Rhabdomyosarcoma including subtypes, using PolyA libraries."
- "Which Tier 1 fusion pairs occur in at least two patients in this project?"
- "Show all fusion pairs, including single-patient events."
- "Show the expression of ALK, FGFR4, and MYCN in a table."
- "Make a violin plot of ALK expression by diagnosis, using log2(TPM + 1), ordered by median descending."
- "List annotated ALK somatic variants, with VAF at least 0.1 and somatic Tier 1."

These examples describe requests, not results for a particular dataset. Use an authorized project or diagnosis in global chat.

## Viewer pages, tables, and plots

A plain "show expression" request for one project may open its expression viewer. Ask explicitly for a table, summary, comparison, or plot when that is the intended result. A simple gene fusion, mutation, or CNV viewing request may open the corresponding portal page; a filtered count or combined analysis uses data tools.

The assistant can show supporting tables, expression plots, and analysis images returned by tools. Check the cohort and filters in the supporting result before using a number from the summary. Large tables and previews can be shortened; a preview is not the complete dataset.

## Follow-up questions and conversation history

Use a follow-up such as "group by diagnosis" when continuing the same analysis. Naming a different gene or assay starts a new request for that subject. Use **New chat** to start a separate conversation, or select a previous conversation from the history control. **Enter** sends a question; **Shift+Enter** inserts a line break.

If a connection ends before the answer completes, the displayed partial text is not proof that the analysis finished. Retry or inspect the supporting execution status. See [troubleshooting](16.-Troubleshooting-and-reproducibility).

## Tutorial answers and tiering diagrams

Ask "How do I download expression matrices?" or "What do the fusion tiers mean?" The assistant retrieves relevant wiki text and cites its source pages.

Tier-definition answers can embed the existing germline, somatic, and fusion tier diagrams. Click a diagram to open the full-size image. If mutation tiering is unspecified, germline and somatic diagrams are both relevant. Displaying the figure does not mean the chatbot has transcribed its image-only criteria. Exact thresholds and exceptions require the figure or a reviewed textual transcription.

Tutorial examples and screenshots are not evidence of a mutation, fusion, or count in your own project. For actual results, the assistant must use an authorized data tool.

pages.title: 11. Cohorts filters and counts
pages.markdown:
# Cohorts, filters, and interpreting counts

## Project versus cancer type

A project is a named data collection. A cancer-type cohort is a diagnosis assembled from the projects available to the current user. The two can have different membership even when their names look similar.

In global chat, identify which kind you mean. In a fixed project page, retain that project and apply a diagnosis filter within it. Cancer-type tools use the exact diagnosis returned by the cancer-type resolver. Abbreviations should be resolved, not guessed.

## Patient, case, and sample are different units

| Unit | Meaning in the portal |
| --- | --- |
| Patient | Subject or cell line identifier; may have multiple cases and samples. |
| Case | A specimen/time point or experiment represented under a patient. |
| Sample | An assay-specific record, for example an RNAseq library. |
| Variant record | An annotated variant occurrence; multiple records may belong to one patient. |
| Fusion pair/tier | A grouped fusion result, with a distinct-patient count for that pair and tier. |

Ask for **distinct patients** when that is the intended denominator. Sample counts, variant rows, and table row counts are not interchangeable with patient counts. A patient may appear in several genes, fusion pairs, or tiers, so summing those counts overestimates unique patients.

## Sample filters

Sample queries can filter assay type (`exp_type`), library type (`library_type`), and diagnosis. The project sample query requires an assay type. Use the exact available values when possible.

Diagnosis matching defaults to exact matching. An explicit contains match can include diagnosis subtypes; for example, a request for Rhabdomyosarcoma including subtypes should say so. Do not infer diagnosis from a sample ID. The supporting sample list and reported counts must reflect the same filters.

## Fusion summary cutoff

The combined fusion cohort detail query supports projects and exact cancer types. A gene is optional, so it can list fusion pairs across the cohort.

`cutoff` means the **inclusive minimum number of distinct patients per fusion pair/tier**. It defaults to **2**. It is not a read-support threshold, minimum number of samples, or maximum number of returned rows.

- `cutoff=2`: retain pair/tier groups seen in at least two distinct patients.
- `cutoff=1`: include single-patient fusion groups.

Repeated samples from the same patient do not increase that patient's contribution to a pair/tier count. Gene and partner filters accept either orientation for the combined detail tool. Caller filtering matches the caller name, not any arbitrary text inside a support field. A separate call-level project tool can use directed left/right partners; state whether direction matters.

## Mutation tiers and annotated details

Mutation gene summaries count distinct patients by gene and tier. Detailed mutation queries return annotated variant records and provide separate full-result patient and sample counts. A detail query is not automatically restricted to pathogenic variants.

Choose the variant type and tier context explicitly. Germline and somatic tiers are separate fields; a Tier 1 filter should say which context is intended. VAF filters use a fraction from 0 to 1: `0.1` means 10%, not 0.1%.

See the [case tiering figures](6.-Cases#variant-tiering), [fusion figure](6.-Cases#output-table), and [programmatic examples](15.-Programmatic-access-and-MCP).

## Empty or partial results

No rows can mean that filters excluded the data, that an assay is unavailable, or that the account lacks access. It does not automatically mean that every patient tested negative. Check the threshold, assay, caller, diagnosis matching, genome build, and permissions before changing the biological interpretation.

pages.title: 12. Expression and differential expression
pages.markdown:
# Expression plots and differential expression

## Select the expression question

Use the project **Expression** views for gene expression, PCA, heatmaps, downloads, and related analyses where available. ChIP-seq peak signal is a different assay and should not be substituted for RNA expression.

A chatbot request for expression values can return per-sample TPM and statistics. Multi-gene queries accept up to 50 gene symbols and align the values by sample; a missing value is reported as missing rather than a measured zero. Genome build and tumor/normal tissue selection may change which samples and values are available.

## Multi-gene viewer and plots

For a project, a plain "show expression of ALK, FGFR4 and MYCN" request can open the expression viewer with those genes. Ask for a table or statistical summary to receive a data result instead of that navigation action.

Plot requests can specify a heatmap, boxplot, violin, barplot, or column plot, plus a metadata grouping such as diagnosis. State the transform and order explicitly:

- `none`: show the returned expression scale.
- `log2p1`: plot log2(value + 1); for TPM this is log2(TPM + 1).
- `zscore`: standardize the plotted expression values; this is not a fold change between experimental groups.
- `median_asc` or `median_desc`: order metadata groups by the median of the plotted values.

For example: "Make a violin plot of ALK TPM by diagnosis using log2(TPM + 1), with groups ordered by median descending."

Violin density estimation requires more than one value in a group. Plot limits and missing values can affect what is drawn; inspect the accompanying explanation and table. A difference in a descriptive expression plot is not itself a differential-expression test.

## Download expression matrices

Open the project, choose **Expression**, then **Download**. Select the matrix type and genome build offered by that project. Count matrices and normalized-expression matrices serve different purposes; preserve the original sample identifiers and record which file was used.

The project interface may offer TPM, TMM-normalized expression, counts, and isoform outputs depending on available processed files. Do not substitute a TPM or FPKM matrix for the count input required by the implemented DESeq2 comparison.

## Fusion-defined DESeq2 comparisons

The chatbot/MCP differential-expression tool currently compares **two RNA-seq sample groups within one project**, defined using exact left/right fusion partners, positive or negative fusion status, and optional diagnosis and caller filters. It is not a general arbitrary-group or cross-project analysis tool.

Before running it, inspect the project's available diagnoses, fusion callers, and count matrices with the cohort schema tool. Define both groups explicitly. "Fusion-negative" means that the sample lacks that exact pair within the selected filters; it does not mean the sample lacks every fusion.

Each group needs at least two resolved RNA-seq samples by default. The groups must not overlap. Count-matrix matching can exclude samples not found in the matrix; inspect included-group counts and missing-sample information rather than assuming all selected records were analyzed. Multiple samples can belong to one patient: sample counts are not distinct-patient counts.

The implemented analysis uses a project count matrix and DESeq2 with a group-only design (`~ group`). It rounds nonnegative expected counts, combines rows with the same gene label, removes genes with total count below 10, tests an absolute log2 fold-change threshold of 1, and applies normal log2-fold-change shrinkage. These are implementation details to record for reproducibility, not universal recommendations for every study design. Paired samples or batch/covariate adjustments require a separately reviewed analysis design.

Positive log2 fold change means higher expression in **group A** than **group B**. The default adjusted-p-value cutoff is 0.05. The response includes ranked gene results, tested/significant-gene counts, the selected thresholds, and a volcano plot when generated. The volcano plot uses shrunken log2 fold change on the horizontal axis and negative log10 adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. Record group definitions, included samples, input matrix/build, parameters, and software versions for a manuscript.

See [counts and cohort definitions](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts) and [troubleshooting](16.-Troubleshooting-and-reproducibility).

pages.title: 13. ChIP seq and chromatin
pages.markdown:
# ChIP-seq and chromatin views

## Start with the assay and target

ChIP-seq describes chromatin-associated enrichment and peaks. RNAseq expression describes transcript abundance. A histone-mark or transcription-factor ChIP-seq result should not be described as gene-expression TPM.

Open the project's ChIP-seq views when ChIP-seq data are available. Project and cancer-type summaries can include sample QC, mapping, duplication, peaks, and super-enhancer metrics. The precise columns depend on the processed data. In the chatbot, name the cohort and target, for example "Show H3K27ac ChIP-seq QC for this project."

## Target-specific matrices and downloads

The ChIP-seq sample interface groups available peak matrices by target. Select the target tab, inspect the displayed and total row counts, and use that tab's **Download** button for the matrix. A target with no processed peaks may have no matrix even if a related assay is listed elsewhere.

Choose the same target and cohort when comparing the table to another view. A filtered table preview or one page of peaks is not a total patient count. Record the target, sample IDs, build, normalization/column units, and source files before comparing signal across samples.

## Browser and detailed results

Where available, ChIP-seq pages link to sample-level views, QC outputs, IGV tracks, super-enhancer plots, and motif results. Availability depends on the relevant files having been processed and on permission to access those samples. Use the genome build associated with the tracks when interpreting coordinates.

If a browser track is missing, first check the sample, target, build, and file availability. An empty browser does not establish lack of a biological signal. See [troubleshooting](16.-Troubleshooting-and-reproducibility).

pages.title: 14. Oncoprint and cBioPortal
pages.markdown:
# Oncoprint and cBioPortal

## Project Oncoprint

Open the project's **Oncoprint** tab where available. The current view summarizes **Tier 1 mutations and fusions**. It is not an exhaustive representation of all tiers or every possible alteration type.

The **Matrix** view has patients in rows and alteration columns. A check mark means that a matching alteration is recorded; a blank means that no matching alteration is recorded in this matrix. The matrix places mutations before fusions and sorts within those groups by patient count.

The **Plot** view places patients in columns and alterations in rows. Green represents mutations, purple represents fusions, and light gray represents no matching recorded alteration. Use the patient search and alteration-type control to narrow the display. Hover for details, drag to zoom, double-click to reset, and use the plot toolbar to pan or save an image.

Large plots show up to 250 patients and 50 alterations per page; use the **Previous** and **Next** controls for each dimension to see more. Row order and percentages reflect the patients matching the plot filters, rather than only the current plot page.

Use **Download TSV** to export all matching patients from the matrix table, rather than treating the current plot page as the complete cohort. Retain the project, tier restriction, and filters with the exported file.

A blank cell does not by itself prove a patient was assayed successfully and found negative. Check the underlying mutation/fusion records, assay coverage, and case availability if that distinction matters.

## cBioPortal links

For configured projects, the project **Summary** includes a **View in cBioPortal** link. The patient listing can also contain an external cBioPortal icon for a mapped patient. These links appear only when the project has a configured study mapping; their absence is not an application error for an unmapped project.

The destination is a separate application with its own availability, access rules, study identifiers, and data refresh schedule. Confirm the study and patient before comparing results. A cBioPortal link does not guarantee that its study snapshot is identical to the current Oncogenomics dataset.

pages.title: 15. Programmatic access and MCP
pages.markdown:
# Programmatic access and MCP

## Authentication and authorization

The Oncogenomics MCP endpoint is `/mcp/onco` relative to the deployed application base URL. It uses a bearer token issued for MCP access. Tokens mapped to an application user inherit that user's project access. Obtain credentials from the application administrator; do not paste credentials into a tutorial, chat message, notebook committed to Git, or shared URL.

MCP credentials are separate from the legacy site download/sync credentials and from the OpenAI or Gemini API keys used by the chatbot. Possessing an LLM API key does not grant access to patient data.

Discover the currently advertised tools and schemas after connecting. Reconnect if a client has cached an older tool catalog. This page describes a workflow, not a guarantee that every tool is enabled on every deployment.

## Resolve the cohort before querying

For a project, call `getProjects` with a name query and `match=exact`, then use the returned authorized numeric ID. For a cancer type, call `getCancerTypes` and use its exact returned Cancer Type value. Never construct project IDs from examples or assume that the same name has the same numeric ID on another instance.

Cohort tools accept `cohort_type=project` or `cohort_type=cancer_type` and the corresponding `cohort_id`. A fixed website chatbot supplies those fields from its page context. A standalone MCP client must supply the resolved values itself.

## Common tools

| Task | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Find an authorized project or diagnosis | `getProjects`, `getCancerTypes` |
| Filter assay samples | `getCohortSamples` |
| Retrieve one or several genes' TPM values | `getCohortExpression` |
| Summarize mutation genes by tier | `getCohortMutationGenes` |
| Retrieve annotated sample-level variants | `getCohortMutationDetails` |
| List fusion pairs by tier and patient cutoff | `getFusionCohortDetail` |
| Inspect ChIP-seq QC and target metrics | `getCohortChIPseq` |
| Discover project diagnoses/callers/count matrices | `getCohortSchema` |
| Run the supported fusion-defined RNA-seq comparison | `runDifferentialExpression` |
| Search the portal's user guide | `searchOncogenomicsWiki` |

Some tools open viewer pages, while others return rows or statistics. For counts, filtering, joins, or reproducible exports, choose a data tool instead of assuming a viewer redirect contains the result.

## Compact responses and pagination

Supported table tools accept an `output` object. Use `mode=compact` for columns and rows, or `mode=summary` for full filtered counts without transmitting rows. Omit `output` when a tool's plot contract requires the full UI result.

A compact page reports `total_rows`, `returned_rows`, and `next_offset`. `total_rows` counts table rows, not unique patients. Follow `next_offset` with the same cohort and filters until it is null; do not infer a total from the first page. `fields` selects exact returned column titles. Invalid field names produce an error rather than silently changing the requested schema.

For example, the `output` part of a sample-list request can be:

```json
{"mode":"compact","limit":100,"offset":0}
```

This is only the output argument, not a complete tool call; also provide the resolved cohort and assay type. Many compact tables default to 100 rows with a maximum of 1000, but follow each tool's advertised limits. Pagination queries the current data and is not a frozen database snapshot.

## Mutation details and fusion summaries

Mutation details can filter gene, type, build, sample, tier context, tier, and minimum VAF. The default mutation-detail page is 100 records. Named patient/sample counts cover the full filtered result; returned rows cover only the page. Missing annotations are null.

Fusion cohort detail defaults to `cutoff=2` distinct patients per pair/tier. Set 1 for single-patient groups. This threshold is independent of output pagination. The older diagnosis-only fusion detail tool remains for compatibility; prefer the combined cohort tool for new integrations.

See [count interpretation](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts) and [expression analysis](12.-Expression-and-differential-expression).

pages.title: 16. Troubleshooting and reproducibility
pages.markdown:
# Troubleshooting and reproducibility

## I cannot see a project, patient, or case

Check the signed-in account, project membership, selected project, and requested case. The same patient can have different cases in different projects. Ask an administrator to review permissions when necessary; do not use another user's credentials or assume that a public-looking project name grants access.

## A tab or download is missing

Tabs depend on the cohort's available assays, configured features, and processed files. Compare the sample/assay list to the requested analysis. A missing ChIP-seq result cannot be replaced by RNAseq expression, and a missing count matrix cannot be replaced by a normalized-expression matrix for DESeq2.

## A filtered query returns no rows

Check these in order:

1. Correct project versus exact cancer-type cohort.
2. Assay and genome build.
3. Exact diagnosis versus an explicitly requested subtype/contains match.
4. Library type, fusion caller, and gene/partner filters.
5. Tier context and threshold. Fusion summaries omit single-patient groups by default because cutoff is 2.
6. Whether the underlying data and annotations are available.

State "no matching recorded results under these filters" when that is what was measured. Do not turn an execution error, missing annotation, or absence from a preview into a confirmed negative result.

## My counts disagree

Check whether the figures count patients, cases, assay samples, variants, genes, or pair/tier groups. Deduplicate at the intended unit. Multiple samples can come from one patient, and a patient can contribute to several genes or fusion pairs. Compare the same cohort, filters, and data snapshot. Page lengths and truncated chatbot previews are not full-cohort totals.

## My chatbot question opens a page

Simple viewer requests may navigate to an analysis page. Add "in a table", "summarize", "count distinct patients", or the desired plot type when you want a data answer. For instructions, ask "How do I ...?" so the assistant searches the tutorial. A tutorial answer may cite a page or display a tiering figure without having retrieved your project's data.

## The chatbot stops or reports an error

Check whether the answer completed and whether the supporting tool succeeded. A timeout or partial streamed answer is not a completed analysis. A model/provider handoff may continue from completed tool results, but the final status and supporting evidence remain the basis for interpretation. If a failure persists, report the question, cohort, time, and visible error without including tokens or private data in a public issue.

## Information to preserve for a manuscript or shared analysis

Record the project/diagnosis and resolved cohort, extraction date, assay and genome build, input files or matrix identifier, gene symbols, variant type/tier context, filters and cutoffs, sample/patient counts and exclusions, software/pipeline versions, annotation database versions, normalization or transforms, and statistical tests and multiple-testing procedures actually used.

For differential expression, also record group membership, direction of the comparison, missing/overlapping sample handling, design formula, count filtering, effect-size threshold, shrinkage, and adjusted-p-value cutoff. The chatbot's model name and prose summary do not establish the scientific method. Use the actual pipeline/configuration/output and review the interpretation with the analyst.

pages.title: 17. Operations and wiki maintenance
pages.markdown:
# Operations, credentials, and wiki maintenance

This page is for administrators and analysts maintaining a deployment. User-facing analysis steps are in the linked topic guides. Site-specific paths, schedules, database connections, and server permissions should be checked against the deployment rather than copied blindly from older screenshots or examples.

## Public data synchronization

The sync page is restricted to superadministrators. Its project lists are fetched through server-side requests; site tokens must not be embedded in browser JavaScript. The internal project list uses the local application. The public project-list request uses a configured sync runtime.

A local sync runtime can point to production database/files without being the web server behind the public website. Keep that distinction explicit:

- `URL_PUBLIC` identifies the public website used for public links.
- Optional `PUBLIC_SYNC_URL` selects the runtime used for public project-list sync requests; if absent, the application falls back to `URL_PUBLIC`.
- The initiating application's `PUBLIC_TOKEN` must match the sync runtime's `TOKEN`.

An authenticated project-list response proves that this part of the connection works. It does not mean a transfer job has run or finished. The existing sync action submits a backend job; inspect its job status and deployment logs when confirming that data were copied.

## Site credentials and download clients

`TOKEN` authenticates legacy token-protected variant/CNV downloads and the POST project-list endpoint. Use a long, randomly generated value in the deployment's ignored `.env` file. Tokens must be nonempty; failed authentication returns a generic error, never the expected credential.

The project-list endpoint accepts bearer authentication and the legacy body credential for compatibility. Legacy download clients may still place a token in a URL, which can appear in request logs; treat those URLs as credentials. Backend clients must read the intended deployment configuration, and an inherited environment variable can override a file-based value. A shared scripts directory does not prove that it reads the same `.env` as the website.

When rotating credentials, update each intended runtime/client and the matching `PUBLIC_TOKEN`/`TOKEN` pair, clear the affected Laravel configuration cache, and verify authentication without printing credentials. Keep MCP bearer tokens, LLM API keys, and institutional sign-in credentials separate. Removing a leaked credential from Git history does not revoke it; rotate it and follow the hosting provider's sensitive-data cleanup procedure where needed.

## Edit and refresh the wiki

The wiki is its own Git repository. A convenient local checkout is `docs/wiki` under the application directory, ignored by the main application's Git rules. Wiki changes are committed/pushed from that checkout to the wiki repository, not staged as a nested repository in the application.

After editing or pulling the wiki, rebuild the chatbot search index from that working tree:

```sh
php artisan chatbot:refresh-wiki --source=docs/wiki
```

The command atomically replaces the runtime index. Failed refreshes preserve the prior index. The application also carries a bundled snapshot for deployments without a refreshed runtime index. A refresh reads local wiki text; it does not train a model or automatically transcribe images.

Review and publish wiki edits separately. New GitHub page links may not resolve until the wiki changes are pushed. When the index includes local edits, it should be treated as a local documentation snapshot rather than a claim that those edits are already public.

pages.title: 18. Gene sets and annotations
pages.markdown:
# Gene sets and annotation badges

## What a gene-list annotation means

Several result tables annotate genes using curated or user-visible gene lists. A list-membership icon answers whether a gene appears in that list. It is different from the observed variant or fusion call, read support, copy-number estimate, clinical classification, or the germline/somatic tier assigned to a particular event.

User-visible lists can depend on the signed-in account, shared/public lists, and the analysis type. Record the list name and its version/source when using a list as a study filter. This guide does not freeze a current list of genes or prescribe a clinical interpretation.

## Hotspot genes

The case CNV views can show a **Hotspot Genes** column alongside the genes in a segment. It highlights membership in the deployment's hotspot gene list. A gene name in that column is not evidence, by itself, of a hotspot sequence variant: review the relevant variant calls and coordinates separately.

For a reproducible analysis, distinguish a list-based CNV annotation from a variant-level hotspot filter and save which list/filter was applied.

## Sanger and Mitelman fusion genes

The case fusion tutorial uses a flame icon for membership in the curated Sanger/Mitelman fusion-gene annotation. This identifies an annotated partner gene, not proof that the exact observed pair is validated or clinically significant. Review the pair, orientation, transcript, caller/support, and tier in the [case fusion output](6.-Cases#output-table).

## Clinomics cancer genes

The case fusion tutorial uses a red-circle icon for membership in the Clinomics cancer-gene annotation. This is a gene-list badge and should not be substituted for the fusion event's tier or a sample-level variant classification.

## Gene-list filters and expression analyses

Where a table offers gene-list filtering, record the selected list together with cohort, assay, build, and other filters. For fusion records, check whether a filter matches either partner or a directed left/right pair. For expression and enrichment analyses, record both the input gene set and the measured/ranked data used by the analysis.

See [cohort filters and counts](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts) for units and [reproducibility](16.-Troubleshooting-and-reproducibility) for the analysis record.

pages.title: 2. Access Control
pages.markdown: # Authentication Use the external sign-in provider offered by your deployment. NIH/PIV and federated sign-in screens depend on the instance's authentication configuration; older screenshots may show a previous provider. Signing in identifies the user but does not automatically grant private-project membership. ## First time user When log on to Oncogenomics first time, the users should see a registration form. This will help us know who the users are and if the access permissions should be granted. Please provide the projects/protocol you are interested in. You can skip this step if you are only interested in public datasets. # Authorization The access control of Oncogenomics is project-based. The minimum access unit is cases. Only authorized users can access private projects. Public projects are open to all the users. ### Add users to projects If you have superadmin privilege, you can add users to projects by following steps: **Step 1**: Go to administration console by clicking your ID: **Step 2**: In administration console, search the user **Step 3**: Click "Edit" icon **Step 4**: In "Edit User" page, the current granted projects and roles will be shown. Click the drop-down menu and Select the project you want to add to the user **Step 5**: Click **Step 6**: Wait for the successful message (**This will refresh the internal view and might take up to 20 seconds**). You should see the message like: The user will receive a notification email about this change. ## Chatbot, API, and administrative access The website chatbot uses the signed-in user's existing project permissions. A general tutorial question does not require choosing a data cohort, but actual project results remain restricted to authorized records. Standalone MCP clients use separately issued bearer credentials mapped to an application user; a chatbot provider API key is not a data-access credential. Public-sync administration is restricted to superadministrators. Its site credentials remain on the server rather than being sent to the browser. See [operations](17.-Operations-and-wiki-maintenance) for the distinction between a public website and a sync runtime.

pages.title: 3. Search
pages.markdown: In Oncogenomics home, users can search * Gene symbol * Patient ID * MRN (medical record number) search if users have permission to do so. * Sample ID * Project name ![](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/search.png) ## LabMatrix search If granted, users are able to search patients with medical record number(MRN) or names. The Clinomics ID will be shown on the screen and users can click the link to the patient page. Note the MRNs will not be displayed for the privacy concerns. ## Selecting a cohort and interpreting search results Choose the intended project before comparing patients or cases. Project membership and case visibility may differ for the same patient across projects. In the chatbot, explicitly say whether a name refers to a project or a cancer type. If several authorized matches are returned, choose one instead of guessing its numeric ID. Diagnosis queries use the authorized Cancer Type values. A subtype is not automatically equivalent to a broader disease name; state explicitly when you want a contains/subtype match within a project. The [cohort guide](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts) explains the filtering and count consequences. For "how do I" questions, use [tutorial chat](10.-Chatbot-and-tutorials) rather than a patient or gene search. Example: "How do I download expression matrices?"

pages.title: 4. Projects
pages.markdown: A project includes a set of patients or cell line experiments. The project views provide the statistics for the whole cohort and help users identify important events with integrated user interface. # Summary The summary tab shows the meta data statistics. Oncogenomics automatically determines if the data types is categorical or numeric and shows bar chart or pie chart respectively. If the project has diagnoses >= 10, a sortable table will be displayed. Users can move the mouse over the bar/pie area to see the detailed patient count. By clicking them, a patient table will show up. Users can view the patient pages by selecting the links. # Patients A patient table including all the meta data. By clicking , the sample list will be displayed. # Mutations The mutations tab shows the summary of the mutations called in the project categorized into the following types: 1. **Germline**: for paired tumor/normal DNA-seq, the variants specific to normal sample. 2. **Somatic**: for paired tumor/normal DNA-seq, the variants specific to tumor sample. 3. **Tumor**: the variants for tumor only DNA-seq samples. 4. **RNAseq**: the RNAseq variants. The summary table includes the gene name and the patient count for each tier. The gene name links will direct users to gene summary page. The number in the tiering columns refer to how many patients have mutations in the genes. The link takes users to the gene level mutation pages. The results can be filtered by MAF, coverage, VAF and meta data. # TIL This tab shows the table summary of the T-cell infiltration using TcellExTRECT. The detailed explanation of the content can be found in [case](6.-Cases#TIL) wiki page. The table can be filtered by the minimum T-cell fraction. # Gene fusions The project level fusion tab summarizes all fusions found in the project. The loading time may be a bit longer if the number of fusions is big. In addition to the left/right gene names and chromosomes, the table shows the patient count grouped by tiering and fusion types. The detailed information is available in [case](6.-Cases#Fusions) wiki page. # Expression The project level expression tab shows the the principal component analysis and heatmap plot. ## PCA: The pre-calculated PCA is based on 1000 genes with highest variation. The values are log2-CPM. This 3D plot can be colored by meta data. Users can also use z-scored or log2 values. Each dot represents an RNAseq sample. By clicking "show labels", the sample ID will be displayed. This might take a while if the number of samples is large. The loading and the total variance will also be shown on the side panel. ![pca](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8780990/161629041-03c5400b-5f1f-4a84-b8f8-b7bc0edd5aaf.png) ## Heatmap: This tab shows the expression heatmap. User can switch the value types to TMM-normalized FPKM or TPM. The order can be sorted by either genes or samples by clicking them. The detailed information will be shown as a popup window when the cursors move to the cells. When clicking , the window will show the sorted scatter and box plots. ## Download: Users can download expression matrices in this tab. This is particularly useful when users need the raw count data to perform downstream analyses such as differential expression analysis. # CNV In summary tab, Oncogenomics summarizes Sequenza results for each case. Each row represents a case. The definition of columns can be found in [case](6.-Cases#Sequenza) wiki page. In download tab, there are four types data can be downloaded: 1. Sequenza summary: the summary information as in summary tab. 2. Sequenza files: a zipped file of all the Sequenza output files in the project. 3. Sequenza matrix file: Sequenza CNV file in matrix format. Rows are gene and columns are samples. The values are CN defined in Sequenza. 4. CNVkit matrix file: CNVkit CNV file in matrix format. Rows are gene and columns are samples. The values are log ratio defined in CNVkit. # Survival analysis Where survival data are available, select the offered analysis, expression measure, genome build, and diagnosis. The expression-survival view offers overall or event-free outcomes, TPM or TMM-normalized expression, and diagnosis selection. Record the actual grouping/cutoff, included population, and statistical output shown by the analysis. Missing outcomes can change the analyzed cohort; a displayed association does not establish causality. # QC Use the available QC summaries to inspect assay-specific quality metrics before interpreting a missing or unexpected result. QC columns differ by assay and processed outputs. A missing value can indicate unavailable QC output rather than failed QC. # Additional project workflows - **Chatbot:** ask scoped questions, request supporting tables and plots, or search the tutorial. The selected project is fixed for data queries. See [chatbot examples](10.-Chatbot-and-tutorials). - **Oncoprint:** inspect the Tier 1 mutation/fusion matrix or interactive plot and download matching patients as TSV. See [Oncoprint](14.-Oncoprint-and-cBioPortal). - **ChIP-seq:** inspect QC and target-specific matrices; this is separate from RNA expression. See [ChIP-seq](13.-ChIP-seq-and-chromatin). - **Expression:** request aligned values for several genes, descriptive plots, or the supported fusion-defined DESeq2 comparison. See [expression analysis](12.-Expression-and-differential-expression). - **cBioPortal:** a configured project can show a study link in Summary and patient links in its patient table. Availability and refresh timing belong to that external application. - **PacBio/isoforms:** long-read and isoform sections/downloads appear only where the project has the corresponding outputs. When using a cancer-type view, remember that it can span multiple authorized projects; it is not automatically the same cohort as a similarly named project. Fusion detail queries default to at least two distinct patients per pair/tier. See [counts and filters](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts).

pages.title: 5. Patients
pages.markdown: In Oncogenomics, patients could be clinical subjects or research cell lines. One patient might consist of multiple cases which represent different tumor samples or research experiments. The patient pages allow users to track all cases in single interface. This is an example of a cell line TT. On the top section, it provides the basic information about this patient/cell line. * Project list. One patient might belong to multiple projects. Here we displayed a granted project list. In this example, the cell line TT belongs to "All Cell Lines", "MTC" and "MTC\__Vandetani_b\_resistance". The current project in the page is "MTC\__Vandetani_b\_resistance". * Diagnosis. The diagnosis of this patient/cell line. In this example, it is Medullary thyroid carcinoma. * Patient ID. The ID of patient of cell line. Please note different projects might contain different cases for the same patient. If you cannot see the cases of interested, you should check if the project selected is correct. You can always switch project by clicking the "Switch Projects" drop-down menu. If a patient has multiple cases, a "merged" at the end provides a combined information for all the cases. ## Working across cases and assays Verify the selected project, patient, case, sample, and genome build when opening a detailed result. Multiple RNAseq or ChIP-seq samples from one patient are multiple assay records, not additional patients. A merged case view summarizes available records and does not imply that every assay was run at every time point. Configured project patient tables may include an external cBioPortal link. Verify its study and patient identifiers before comparing results, since it can represent a separately refreshed dataset. See [external links](14.-Oncoprint-and-cBioPortal).

pages.title: 6. Cases
pages.markdown: A case view contains assay-specific result panels. Available panels depend on the processed data and permissions. Verify patient, case, sample, and genome build before interpreting a result. # Table of Contents - [Summary](#summary) - [Mutation tabs](#mutation-tabs) * [Mutation types](#mutation-types) * [Variant filtering](#variant-filtering) * [Variant tiering](#variant-tiering) + [Germline](#germline) + [Somatic](#somatic) * [Variant annotations](#variant-annotations) - [CNV](#cnv) * [Sequenza](#sequenza) * [CNVkit](#cnvkit) - [TIL](#til) - [Fusions](#fusions) * [Output table](#output-table) - [Expression](#expression) - [Signature](#signature) - [HLA](#hla) - [Neoantigen](#neoantigen) - [Circos](#circos) - [Download](#download) - [QC](#qc) *** ## Summary * **Pipeline version** * **Samples** Sample list has the following columns: * **Sample**: sample name. * **DNA/RNA** * **Experiment type**: exome/panel/RNAseq/ChIPseq/HiC * **Platform**: Illumina or others * **Library type**: this could be capture kit version or RNAseq library preparation methods (polyA, Access or ribozero) * **Tumor/Normal** * Other project specific columns. * **Coverage summary plot:** A cumulative coverage plot. * **Mutation summary plot:** A bar plot grouped by variant types and tiers. ## Mutation tabs ![](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/mutation.png) ### Mutation types 1. **Germline**: for paired tumor/normal DNA-seq, the variants specific to normal sample. 2. **Somatic**: for paired tumor/normal DNA-seq, the variants specific to tumor sample. 3. **Tumor**: the variants for tumor only DNA-seq samples. 4. **RNAseq**: the RNAseq variants. 5. **Hotspots**: the variants for hotspot mutations only. ### Variant filtering There are several ways to filter out unwanted variants. 1. **Gene sets**: Use "**Add filter**" button to filter the variants by gene sets. 2. **Show all**: All filtering conditions will be removed. 3. **Reset**: The default cut-off will be restored. 4. **MAF (Minor allele frequency)**: The upper limit of MAF will keep the rare variants only. 5. **Min Total Cov (Minimum total coverage)**: This cut-off will filter out low coverage variants. 6. **Min VAF (Minimum VAF)**: This cut-off will filter out the variants with low VAF. 7. **Tier**: Only the tiers selected will be shown. 8. **Flag**: Only flagged variants will be displayed. 9. **No FP**: Do not show the false positive variants. These are highly recurrent variants in ClinOmics project. 10. **High Conf**: High confident variants. The definition: * **Germline calls**: Only from Haplo caller * **Panel and Exome** * Total coverage > 20x and * Fisher score < 75 and * VAF >= 0.25 * **Somatic calls**: Only from Mutect and Strelka * **Exome** * Tumor total coverage >=20x and * Normal total coverage >=20x and * VAF >= 0.10 * **Panel** * Tumor total coverage >=50x and * Normal total coverage >=20x and * iii. VAF >= 0.05 ### Variant tiering Oncogenomics has separate germline and somatic tiering systems. RNAseq and tumor-only variant views can report both. State which tier context you are filtering; "Tier 1" alone can be ambiguous. The diagrams below are the authoritative visual references in this tutorial. Their image-only criteria have not been transcribed into reviewed searchable rules. For returned counts, distinguish annotated variant records from distinct patients. A VAF filter in the detailed cohort tool uses fractions (0.1 means 10%). See [cohort filters and counts](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts). #### Germline ![](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/Germline-Classification--03022017-1.svg) #### Somatic ### Variant annotations Oncogenomics provides a variety of annotations to help users evaluate the importance of variants. Users can always show/hide columns by clicking "**Select Columns**". The detailed description of these columns: * **Flag**: * : Not flagged * : Might be false positive variant. * : Flagged in other samples. * **ACMG Guide**: A simple ACMG form that help users determine the ACMG classification. See [https://www.acmg.net/ACMG/Medical-Genetics-Practice-Resources/Practice-Guidelines.aspx](https://www.acmg.net/ACMG/Medical-Genetics-Practice-Resources/Practice-Guidelines.aspx) for details. * **Libraries:** By clicking , a caller summary information table will be displayed: * **Sample name**. * **Experiment type**: Exome/Panel/RNAseq. * **Tumor/Normal**. * **Caller**. * **Qual**: Calling quality. * **Fisher score**: the score can be used to determine if strand bias is observed. * **Total coverage**: the total read count. * **Variant coverage:** the read count with variants. * **VAF**: variant allele frequency. * **VAF ratio**: tumor VAF/normal VAF. * **Relation**: the relation to the target patient. * **IGV**: display the IGV viewer. ![](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/igv.png) * **Gene cohort**: the percent of patients having mutations in the same gene. * **Site cohort**: the percent of patients having mutations at the same site. * **Caller**: the caller name. * **Chr**: chromosome of the variant. * **Start**: start position of the variant (1-based) * **End**: end position of the variant * **Ref**: the reference bases * **Alt**: the mutation bases * **Region**: exonic/splicing/UTR or intronic. * **Gene**: gene symbol * **Exonic function:** * **SNV**: nonsynonymous mutations (synonymous mutations are pre-filtered) * **splicing**: splice site mutations * **stopgain**: early stop codon gained * **stoploss**: stop codon mutations * **frameshift** deletion/insertion: in-frame indels * **nonframeshift** deletion/insertion: out-of-frame indels * **AAChange**: amino acids changes * **Pecan**: links to St Jude PeCan ([https://pecan.stjude.cloud/](https://pecan.stjude.cloud)) * **CIViC**: CIViC precision medicine info ([https://civicdb.org/home](https://civicdb.org/home)) * **CLIA Actionable**: Actionable mutations defined in: * **CanDL** * **CLViC** * **My Cancer Genome** * **NCI MATCH Trail** * **dbSNP**: dbSNP links * **MAF (Minor allele frequency)**: the minor allele frequency in known population: * **ExAC/ExAC nonTCGA** ([https://exac.broadinstitute.org/](https://exac.broadinstitute.org)) * **gnomAD** ([https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/](https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org)) * **NCI60** ([https://dtp.cancer.gov/discovery\_development/nci-60/](https://dtp.cancer.gov/discovery\_development/nci-60/)) * **1000 Genome** ([https://www.internationalgenome.org/1000-genomes-summary](https://www.internationalgenome.org/1000-genomes-summary)) * **Prediction**: prediction tool results * **CADD** ([https://cadd.gs.washington.edu/](https://cadd.gs.washington.edu)) * **fathmm** ([http://fathmm.biocompute.org.uk/](http://fathmm.biocompute.org.uk)) * **MA** (MutationAssessor, [http://mutationassessor.org/r3/](http://mutationassessor.org/r3/)) * **PP2HDIV** (PolyPhen-2 HDIV, [http://genetics.bwh.harvard.edu/pph2/](http://genetics.bwh.harvard.edu/pph2/)) * **PP2HVAR** (PolyPhen-2 HVAR, [http://genetics.bwh.harvard.edu/pph2/](http://genetics.bwh.harvard.edu/pph2/)) * **PROVEAN** ([http://provean.jcvi.org/index.php](http://provean.jcvi.org/index.php)) * **SIFT** ([https://sift.bii.a-star.edu.sg/](https://sift.bii.a-star.edu.sg)) * **VEST** ([https://karchinlab.org/apps/appVest.html](https://karchinlab.org/apps/appVest.html)) * **Clinvar**: the Clinvar results: * **Accession** * **Review status:** ([https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/docs/review\_status/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/docs/review\_status/)) * **Significance:** ([https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/docs/clinsig/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/docs/clinsig/)) * **Disease name** * **Pubmed ID** * **VarID:** Varant ID * **Clinvar badged** ([https://www.clinicalgenome.org/tools/clinical-lab-data-sharing-list/](https://www.clinicalgenome.org/tools/clinical-lab-data-sharing-list/)) * **Cosmic**: ([https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/cosmic](https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/cosmic)) * Reported: the number of patients reported mutations from: * **cBioPortal/TCGA:** ([http://www.cbioportal.org/](http://www.cbioportal.org)) * **ICGC** ([https://dcc.icgc.org/](https://dcc.icgc.org)) * **GENIE** ([https://www.aacr.org/professionals/research/aacr-project-genie/aacr-project-genie-data/](https://www.aacr.org/professionals/research/aacr-project-genie/aacr-project-genie-data/)) * **Pediatric Cancer Genome** (compiled by Dr. Javed Khan's lab) * **HGMD** ([http://www.hgmd.cf.ac.uk/ac/index.php](http://www.hgmd.cf.ac.uk/ac/index.php)) * **Intervar** ([https://wintervar.wglab.org/](https://wintervar.wglab.org)) * **OncoKB** ([https://www.oncokb.org/](https://www.oncokb.org)) * **Loss of function**: if variants are: * splicing variants * stopgain/stoploss variants * indels * **Total coverage**: the total read count. * **Variant coverage:** the read count with variants. * **VAF**: variant allele frequency (variant coverage/total coverage). * **VAF ratio**: tumor VAF/normal VAF. * **Matched total coverage**: Matched DNA/RNA read count. * **Normal total coverage**: Matched normal DNA read count. ## CNV Oncogenomics support two CNV tools: Sequenza ([https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sequenza/vignettes/sequenza.html](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sequenza/vignettes/sequenza.html)) and CNVkit ([https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/](https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/)). Sequenza requires tumor/normal paired samples. CNVkit recommends combining all normal samples into a "pooled reference". ### Sequenza Sequenza is a tool to analyze genomic sequencing data from paired normal-tumor samples, including cellularity and ploidy estimation; mutation and copy number (allele-specific and total copy number) detection, quantification and visualization. * **Genome View PDF:** Genome-whide visualization of the allele-specific and absolute copy number results, and raw profile of the depth ratio and allele frequency. ![Allele-specific copy number](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/sequenza\_allele.png) ![Absolute copy number](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/sequenza\_total.png) ![Depth ratio and allele frequency](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/sequenza\_raw.png) * **Chromosome View PDF:** Visualization per chromosome of depth.ratio, B-allele frequency and mutations, using the selected or estimated solution. One chromosome per slide ![](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/sequenza\_chr.png) * **Table View:** The Sequenza CNV table shows the reported CNV segments and associated genes. * **Table columns**: * **Sample ID:** The sample ID * **Chromosome**: The chromosome of the segment * **Start**: The start coordinate of the segment * **End**: The end coordinate of the segment * **Length**: The length of the segment in MB * **CNt**: Estimated total copy number value * **Allele A**: Estimated number of A-alleles * **Allele B**: Estimated number of B-alleles (minor allele) * **Hotspot Genes**: The [hotspot gene list](18.-Gene-sets-and-annotations#hotspot-genes) * **Gene list**: All genes in the segment * **Filtering**: * **Gene set**: Use "Add filter" button to add gene set filtering * **Copy number**: Use "Any", ">=", "<=" or "=" to set the copy number filtering * **Show diploid**: Show diploid segments. * **Gene Centric View**: Instead of showing gene list in a row, this mode will show one gene per row. Users can use this mode if they look for a gene of interest. * **Exact gene search**: By checking "Exact gene match", the search will show exact matches only. This is useful if users do not want to see the partial matched genes. * **Summary information**: * **Length(Non-diploid/Total)**: The ratio of total non-diploid length to the total length. * **A**: Number of non-diploid rows. * **C**: Number of chromosome with non-diploid rows. * **GI**: Genomic index (A/C) * **Segments**: Total number of segments * **Expression plot**: It is useful to see the expression level of the genes. By clicking the gene links in gene list/hotspot genes, a sorted scatter expression plot will be displayed. The big red circle represents the current sample. This plot shows the distribution of the expression level (log(TPM+1)) in the current project. ### CNVkit CNVkit is a software toolkit to infer and visualize copy number from high-throughput DNA sequencing data. It is designed for use with hybrid capture, including both whole-exome and custom target panels, and short-read sequencing platforms such as Illumina and Ion Torrent. * **Genome View**: Scrolling down this tab, users will see the interactive plots for each chromosome. These interactive views were created by [reconCNV](https://github.com/rghu/reconCNV). Users can see the gene list when hovering the mouse pointer over the segment dots. ![reconCNV view](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/cnvkit\_chr.png) * **Table View**: * **Chromosome**: The chromosome of the segment * **Start**: The start coordinate of the segment * **End**: The end coordinate of the segment * **Length**: The length of the segment in MB * **log2**: Weighted mean of log2 ratios of the segment * **Depth**: Weighted mean of un-normalized read depths of the segment * **Probes**: Weighted mean of number of probes in the segment * **Weight**: The sum of the weights of the bins supporting the segment * **Hotspot Genes**: The [hotspot gene list](18.-Gene-sets-and-annotations#hotspot-genes) * **Gene list**: All genes in the segment * **Gene Centric View**: Instead of showing gene list in a row, this mode will show one gene per row. Users can use this mode if they look for a gene of interest. * **Exact gene search**: By checking "Exact gene match", the search will show exact matches only. This is useful if users do not want to see the partial matched genes. * **Expression plot**: It is useful to see the expression level of the genes. By clicking the gene links in gene list/hotspot genes, a sorted scatter expression plot will be displayed. The big red circle represents the current sample. This plot shows the distribution of the expression level (log(TPM+1)) in the current project. ## TIL We use [TcellExTRECT ](https://github.com/McGranahanLab/TcellExTRECT)a WES based tool to estimate T cell fractions. * **Status**: OK or not enough coverage. * **Fraction**: The estimated T cell fraction(0 to 1) * **Purity**: Tumor purity estimated by Sequenza. * **Ploidy**: The tumor ploidy estimated by Sequenza. **TCRA plot**: The visualization output from T Cell ExTRECT. This can be very useful to check that everything is working. The following produces the pre and post GC corrected versions of the log ratio within the TCRA loci, reads are coloured by the class of VDJ segment they are, e.g. TCRA-V segments are blue. Note that the TCRA loci also includes segments related to TCR delta (TCRD or TRD), e.g. TCRD-V. Vertical dotted lines represent the regions of the genome used for the normalised baseline (Norm region start and Norm region end) as well as the 'Focal region' that is used in the calculation of the TCRA fraction as the location we expect to see maximum signal. ([https://github.com/McGranahanLab/TcellExTRECT](https://github.com/McGranahanLab/TcellExTRECT)) ## Fusions Oncogenomics uses [fusionTools](https://github.com/CCRGeneticsBranch/fusionTools) to annotate fusion reports. In short, the features of fusionTools are: 1. Determine the fusion cDNA and protein sequences 2. Determine the fusion type (in-frame, out-of-frame or right gene intact) 3. Tier the importance of the fusion events 4. Visualize the results in html format ### Output table By default, the main table shows the fusion results from **canonical transcripts** (even the canonical transcripts do not output predicted fusion protein products). * **Details**: By clicking , a detailed transcript level table will be displayed. This table is sorted by protein length. Please note the transcript pairs that do not generate fusion protein will not be shown here. Also, it is possible different transcript pairs produce the same protein sequences. ![](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/fusion.png) By clicking another in the detailed table, a fusion plot will be shown: ![](https://github.com/CCRGeneticsBranch/fusionTools/raw/main/plot.png) The plot shows both fusion DNA and proteins. The domains are predicted using Pfam. The bottom of the plot is the predicted cDNA and protein sequence. ![](https://github.com/CCRGeneticsBranch/fusionTools/raw/main/sequences.png) * **IGV**: Checking IGV viewer is always a good way to make sure the fusion event is real. The IGV window will split into two parts: the upstream part will be on the left and downstream part will be on the right. By default, the soft-clipping option is on. The soft-clipping sequences are usually fusion counterpart sequences. ![](https://clinomics.ccr.cancer.gov/clinomics/public/images/tutorial/fusion\_igv.png) * **Left gene:** The gene symbol of left (5 prime end) gene. means this gene belongs to [Sanger curated and Mitelman fusion genes](18.-Gene-sets-and-annotations#sanger-and-mitelman-fusion-genes). means this gene belongs to [Clinomics cancer genes](18.-Gene-sets-and-annotations#clinomics-cancer-genes). * **Right gene**: The gene symbol of right (3 prime end) gene. means this gene belongs to [Sanger curated and Mitelman fusion genes](18.-Gene-sets-and-annotations#sanger-and-mitelman-fusion-genes). means this gene belongs to [Clinomics cancer genes](18.-Gene-sets-and-annotations#clinomics-cancer-genes). * **Left Chr**: The left gene chromosome * **Left Position**: The breakpoint position of left gene. * **Right Chr**: The rihgt gene chromosome * **Right Position**: The breakpoint position of right gene. * **Tools**: The original fusion callers and spanning read count. For Arriba, there will be three numbers: (split reads in left gene, split reads in right gene and discordant reads). The gene to which the longer segment of the split read aligns is defined as the anchor. * **Type**: * **In-frame**: The frame is intact in right gene. * **Out-of-frame**: The frame is shifted in right gene. An early stop codon is expected. * **Right gene intact**: the breakpoint of right gene is before the start codon. These fusion events might produce whole right gene proteins but use the left gene promoters. * **No proteins**. * If no annotated exons and CDS found in either fusion transcripts, the fusion will be reported as "No proteins". * If the breakpoint is in intronic regions, 3/5 UTRs or intergenic regions, no protein sequences will be reported with the following two exceptions: * Right gene intact * The breakpoint is intronic but very close to splice sites (<100bp). In this case, Oncogenomics will try to rescue this fusion by using intronic sequences. * **Var level**: The fusion tiering. * **Left region**: The left breakpoint regions in canonical transcript(exon, introns, UTR or upstream intergenic, downstream intergenic). * **Right region**: The right breakpoint regions in canonical transcript (exon, introns, UTR or upstream intergenic, downstream intergenic). * **Canonical left trans**: The Ensembl canonical transcript accession of the left gene * **Canonical right trans**: The Ensembl canonical transcript accession of the right gene ## Expression Expression tab shows the RNAseq expression level as log2 TPM. If the RNAseq sample has corresponding Exome sample, the Sequenza estimated copy number column will be added to the expression table. By clicking TPM or copy number link, the sorted scatter plot of project level logTPM or copy number will be shown in a popup window. ## Signature We use COSMIC mutational signatures defined in ([https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/signatures/](https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/signatures/)) ## HLA We use two HLA estimation tools: [seq2HLA](https://github.com/TRON-Bioinformatics/seq2HLA) and [HLAminer](https://github.com/bcgsc/HLAminer) High confident HLA are the ones called by both callers. ![hla](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8780990/161334121-042a243e-8e57-4deb-a3ba-f7ac9e64fa77.png) ## Neoantigen For each somatic mutation site, we predict the matched HLA allele and epitopes using [NetMHC](https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/service.php?NetMHC-4.0), [NetMHCpan](https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/service.php?NetMHCpan-4.1) and [NetMHCcons](https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/service.php?NetMHCcons-1.1). We report the wild type, mutant and the corresponding fold change. Users can filter the results by: 1. Minimun fold change 2. High confident prediction: the HLA alleles must be called by both callers. 3. Read count (both Exome or/and RNAseq) Users can also check the mutation spots using our IGV tool. ## Circos Here we present the circos plot, a user-friendly interactive plot to visualize the important mutations, fusions and copy number in the scale of whole genome. The dots represent the germline/somatic Tier1 mutations. The bar plot is the copy number inferred by Sequenza. The lines are Tier 1 and Tier 2 fusions. The associated gene symbols are also labels. ## Download Users can download zipped VCF file from this tab. ## QC Oncogenomics provides detailed QC information: * AVIA versions: We list all the tools/data sources used for variant annotations. * Circos: This is the PNG circos plot for users to easily compare the LOH among different samples. It can also be used to verify the sequencing data is problemetic. * Coverage plot: This plot shows the fraction of capture target bases for each sample. * Transcript coverage plot: This plot shows the coverage of transcript loci. Users can examine if there is strong 5/3 prime bias in the RNAseq data. * Hotspot coverage plots: This box plot shows the coverage of important hotspot sites. * Contours: This plot shows the relationship between cellularity and ploidy. The best and alternative solutions are shown. * Conpair: [Conpair](https://github.com/nygenome/Conpair) is a concordance and contamination estimator for tumor–normal paired samples. * DNA QC: The summary of the Exome QC data. If the text is shown in red color, the value is below the threshold defined. Users can click "QC threshold" to view the cut-offs. * RNAs QC: The full RNAseq QC report. * Genotyping: Genotyping is a useful information to determine if the samples are mislabeled. We show the pairwise similarity among the samples in the case. If the similarity is between 80 ~ 90%, the text will be labeled in purple color. If it is below 80%, the text will be displayed in red color. ## From case details to cohort summaries Use the case view for individual annotated calls and the [project/cancer-type fusion summary](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts#fusion-summary-cutoff) for distinct-patient counts across a cohort. In the combined fusion detail query, the default cutoff of 2 means at least two distinct patients per pair/tier, not two supporting reads. Request cutoff 1 to retain single-patient events. Tier-definition questions in the chatbot can display these germline/somatic diagrams and the fusion-tier figure. The figure opens full-size when clicked; tutorial text should not invent thresholds that appear only inside the image.

pages.title: 7. Upload
pages.markdown: If permission granted, the users can upload cases or clinical meta data through upload pages. # Upload clinical meta data Users can upload meta using a tab separated text file. The file should include a "Patient ID" or "Sample ID" column which can be used to link the current processed data. ### 1. Select "Upload" -> "Clinical data" from the menu. ### 2. Select patient meta data. * Step 1: Click "Choose File" to select the text file to be uploaded. The text file must be tab-separated. The first line should be the header line. * Step 2: Use the drop-down menu to select "Patient ID" column. If the data include the survival information, select the corresponding columns. * Step 3: Check the columns to be included and change the label if needed. * Step 4: Click "Next" ### 3. Select sample meta data (optional) The logic is the same as previous step. Click "Next" to the final step. ### 4. Submit the data Click "Upload" to submit the data. You should see the successful message when it is done. # Validate metadata before and after upload Check that identifier columns refer to the intended existing patients or samples, headers match the intended attributes, and the text is truly tab-separated. Preserve identifier formatting, including any leading zeros. Confirm the selected survival columns and units with the study analyst rather than assuming dates, event codes, or time units from a column name. Upload only attributes and records that the account is authorized to maintain. After the success response, reopen the affected project/patient/sample metadata and verify a few known records and the relevant summary/grouping fields. A successful upload message is not a substitute for checking the resulting metadata.

pages.title: 9. DataSync
pages.markdown:
# Scope of this operational guide

The paths and timed jobs below describe an existing deployment workflow. Verify the actual service-account configuration and scheduler before treating those times as current. This tutorial does not install or change scheduled jobs.

For public project-list sync, credential rotation, the distinction between a local production-data runtime and a public website, and wiki indexing, see [operations and wiki maintenance](17.-Operations-and-wiki-maintenance).

# Data sync
## Description of how Oncogenomics syncs data daily

#### On Biowulf
* At 23:00 daily, a cron job script /data/khanlab/projects/updatedSync/check_processed_runs.sh is launched to gather all newly processed cases from pipeline.
*  The path of project location is defined in /data/khanlab/projects/updatedSync/projects.txt

| Project  | Location        |
|-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| compass_tso500  | /data/Compass/Analysis/ProcessedResults_NexSeq/OncoPilot/        |
| compass_exome   | /data/Compass/Analysis/ProcessedResults_NexSeq/ExomeRNA_Results/ |
| khanlab3        | /data/khanlab3/processed_DATA/                                   |
| clinomics       | /data/khanlab2/ProcessedResults_TGEN/                            |
| wulab           | /data/Wulab/processed_DATA/                                      |
| Acc_19          | /data/Acc_19/processed_DATA/                                     |
| BeatCC          | /data/khanlab3/BeatCC/processed_DATA/                            |
| processed_DATA  | /data/khanlab/projects/processed_DATA/                           |
| roper           | /data/RoperData/processed_DATA/                                  |
| alex            | /data/AlexanderP3/processed_DATA/                                |
| gb              | /data/khanlab3/gb_omics/processed_DATA/                          |
| k2_data         | /data/khanlab3/k2_data_tmp/                                      |
| khanlab2        | /data/khanlab2/processed_DATA/                                   |
| NF_benchmarking | /data/khanlab2/NF_benchmarking/results.processed_data/           |
| GBNCI           | /data/GBNCI/projects/Sanam_Tumor-normal_processed_data/          |

* For each project, three files will be generated in /data/khanlab/projects/updatedSync/update_list2:
  1. new_list_[project name].txt
  2. today_list_[project name].txt
  3. yesterday_list_[project name].txt

* The logic of check_processed_runs.sh:
  1. Copy today_list.txt to yesterday list.txt
  2. Save timestamp (with format "Y") of all successful.txt and failed_delete.txt to today_list.txt using stat command
  3. Save the difference between today_list.txt and yesterday list.txt to new_list.txt

#### On Frederick server (fsabcl-onc03d)
* #### At 2:00 daily, a cron job script "/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/syncProcessedResults.sh all db all" is launched to sync and upload the data to database.
   * Sync "new_list.txt" on biowulf (defined in /var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/project_mapping.txt) to /var/www/html/onco.data/ProcessedResults/update_list
   * For each case, sync data to /var/www/html/onco.data/ProcessedResults/
   * Run script ```/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/deleteCase.pl``` to delete cases with "failed_delete.txt"
   * Run script ```/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/uploadCase.pl``` to upload cases with "successful.txt" to database 
   * Run script ```/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/refreshViews.pl``` to refresh materialized views on Oracle database
   * Run script ```/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/updateVarCases.pl``` to determine the case name (defined in master file) for the processed cases

* #### At 5:00 daily, a cron job script "/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/syncProcessedResults.sh all bam all" is launched to sync BAM files.
* #### At 10:00 daily, a cron job script "/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/syncProcessedResults.sh all tier all" is launched to update variants tiering based on AVIA annotation. (This should be launched after AVIA processing is finished)

## Manually sync data
If pathology users need to sync data manually, please follow the steps:
1. On Biowulf, run ```data/khanlab/projects/updatedSync/check_processed_runs.sh``` to identify new cases
2. SSH to fsabcl-onc03d with service account (ncif-www-onc-svc). 
3. Run ```/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/syncProcessedResults.sh all db all```
4. Run ```/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/syncProcessedResults.sh all bam all```

## Manually upload data to DB
If data is synced but could not find them in database (check if the case_id exists in table processed_cases), then:
1. Go to https://oncogenomics.ccr.cancer.gov/production/public/viewDataIntegrityReport/COMPASS
2. Click "Unloaded cases".
3. Download the file
4. The file is a tab-separated text file with three columns (patient_id/case_id/path)
5. SSH to fsabcl-onc03d with service account (ncif-www-onc-svc).
6. Run ```/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/uploadCases.sh <file>```, where <file> is the downloaded text file.
7. Run ```/var/www/html/clinomics/app/scripts/backend/updateVarCases.pl``` to determine the case name (defined in master file) for the processed

pages.markdown:
# Oncogenomics user guide

Oncogenomics brings project, patient, case, and sample results into one portal. Start with a project or diagnosis, check which assays are available, and then open the relevant analysis. A missing result can mean unavailable data, an active filter, or insufficient permission; it does not by itself establish a negative biological finding.

## Start here

1. [Introduction and data organization](1.-Introduction)
2. [Sign-in and access control](2.-Access-Control)
3. [Search and navigation](3.-Search)
4. [Project and cancer-type views](4.-Projects)
5. [Patients and cases](5.-Patients)
6. [Case results and tiering figures](6.-Cases)
7. [Uploading clinical metadata](7.-Upload)

## Analysis guides

- [Chatbot and tutorial answers](10.-Chatbot-and-tutorials): ask questions, select cohorts, continue a conversation, and view tier diagrams.
- [Cohort filters and interpreting counts](11.-Cohorts-filters-and-counts): distinguish patients, cases, samples, variants, and fusion pairs.
- [Expression plots and differential expression](12.-Expression-and-differential-expression): multi-gene views, transforms, grouping, downloads, and fusion-defined DESeq2 comparisons.
- [ChIP-seq and chromatin](13.-ChIP-seq-and-chromatin): target-specific QC, peak matrices, and browser views.
- [Oncoprint and cBioPortal](14.-Oncoprint-and-cBioPortal): Tier 1 alteration matrices, interactive plots, exports, and external links.
- [Programmatic access and MCP](15.-Programmatic-access-and-MCP): authenticated tools, filters, paging, and output contracts.
- [Troubleshooting and reproducibility](16.-Troubleshooting-and-reproducibility): diagnose empty results and record enough detail to reproduce an analysis.

- [Gene sets and annotation badges](18.-Gene-sets-and-annotations): interpret hotspot and curated-gene annotations separately from event tiers.

## Administration

- [Data synchronization](9.-DataSync)
- [Operations, credentials, and wiki maintenance](17.-Operations-and-wiki-maintenance)
- [Change log](8.-Change-log)

## About this guide

Expanded against the current application checkout on November 4, 2026. Some features depend on the deployed application version, project configuration, processed files, and user permissions. Existing screenshots may show earlier layouts. The text describes available application behavior; it does not replace the source pipeline's versioned methods or establish clinical significance.
